'''John Stanley Edgar''' {{post-nominals|country=NZL|ONZM}} (26 December 1950 – 3 April 2021) was a New Zealand sculptor and [[medallist]].

==Early life and education==
Born in [[Auckland]] on 26 December 1950, Edgar was educated at [[Mount Albert Grammar School]] and then the [[University of New South Wales]].<ref name="NZSO">{{cite web |title=John Edgar |url=http://www.nzsculptureonshore.co.nz/explore/john-edgar |website=NZ Sculpture OnShore |accessdate=1 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190314083317/http://www.nzsculptureonshore.co.nz/explore/john-edgar |archive-date=14 March 2019 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="CAG">{{cite web |title=John Edgar: Lie of the Land |url=https://christchurchartgallery.org.nz/exhibitions/john-edgar-lie-of-the-land |publisher=[[Christchurch Art Gallery]] |accessdate=1 March 2019}}</ref><ref name="Death notice">{{cite news |url=https://notices.nzherald.co.nz/obituaries/nzherald-nz/obituary.aspx?n=john-stanley-onzm-edgar-johno&pid=198254299 |title=John Edgar death notice |date=6 April 2021 |work=New Zealand Herald |access-date=6 April 2021}}</ref> He then worked as a [[research chemist]] and as a [[Prospecting|prospector]] before turning to sculpture.<ref name="CAG" />

==Sculptural work==
As a sculptor, Edgar worked chiefly in hard [[stone]], and occasionally in other materials, such as [[glass]] or [[copper]].<ref name="AFNZ">{{cite web |title=John Edgar – Meet the makers behind our awards |url=https://www.thearts.co.nz/news/john-edgar-meet-the-makers-behind-our-awards |publisher=[[Arts Foundation of New Zealand]] |accessdate=1 March 2019 |date=17 April 2018}}</ref>

In 2000, he designed ''McLeod's Crossing'', a pedestrian bridge over the [[Oratia Stream]] in Falls Park, [[Henderson, New Zealand|Henderson]],<ref name="AFNZ" /><ref>{{Cite web|last=Edgar|first=John|title=Transformer|url=https://www.aucklandpublicart.com/artworks/3598|access-date=2021-08-19|website=Auckland Public Art}}</ref> commissioned by [[Waitakere City Council]]. Since 2004, a public commission, ''Transformer'', has been part of the sculpture walk in the [[Auckland Domain]].<ref name="ET">{{Cite web|last=Edgar|first=John|title=Red Cross|url=https://www.aucklandpublicart.com/artworks/3599|access-date=2021-08-19|website=Auckland Public Art}}</ref> Another work, ''Lie of the Land'', was installed in the [[Savill Garden]], in [[Windsor Great Park]] in England, in 2012.<ref name="KKA">{{cite web |title=The Savill Garden, New Zealand Gardens, Windsor Great Park |url=https://kiwikidsabroad.com/the-savill-garden-windsor-great-park/ |website=Kiwi Kids Abroad |accessdate=1 March 2019}}</ref> His works are also in a number of public collections, including [[Auckland Council]],<ref>{{Cite web|date=19 Aug 2021|title=Search|url=https://www.aucklandpublicart.com/artworks/3599|access-date=2021-08-19|website=Auckland Public Art}}</ref> [[Christchurch Art Gallery]], [[Corning Museum of Glass]] (USA), the [[Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa]] and the [[National Museum of Australia]].<ref name="AFNZ" />

Edgar designed the Icon award medal for the [[Arts Foundation of New Zealand]],<ref name="AFNZ" /> and the medal awarded to Companions of [[Auckland War Memorial Museum]].<ref name="AWMM">{{cite book |title=2018 awards programme notes |publisher=Auckland War Memorial Museum}}</ref> The latter is made from "two New Zealand argillites (pakohe) from the South Island bound together with aluminium".<ref name="AWMM" /> He also illustrated books of poetry by [[Dinah Hawken]].<ref name="Holloway">{{cite web |title=page stone leaf – Dinah Hawken, John Edgar |url=http://www.hollowaypress.auckland.ac.nz/hawken01.htm |publisher=Holloway Press |accessdate=1 March 2019}}</ref><ref name="VUP">{{cite web |title=Ocean and Stone |url=http://vup.victoria.ac.nz/ocean-and-stone/ |publisher=Victoria University Press |accessdate=1 March 2019}}</ref>

== Honours and awards ==
Edgar was appointed an [[Officer of the New Zealand Order of Merit]] in the [[2009 New Year Honours (New Zealand)|2009 New Year Honours]], for services to art, in particular sculpture.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.dpmc.govt.nz/publications/new-year-honours-list-2009 | title=New Year honours list 2009 |date=31 December 2008 | publisher=Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet | access-date=2 March 2019}}</ref>

==Other activities==
Edgar lived in [[Karekare, New Zealand|Karekare]], and served as president of the [[Waitakere Ranges]] Protection Society since 1998.<ref name="WRPS"/> He was made a life member of the society in 2005.<ref name="WRPS">{{cite web |title=Committee Members |url=http://www.waitakereranges.org.nz/members.html |publisher=Waitakere Ranges Protection Society |accessdate=1 March 2019}}</ref> 

==Death==
Edgar died in Auckland on 3 April 2021.<ref name="Death notice"/>
